title: Prospective evaluation of LLM-supported information extraction from medical documents for tumour documentation (LLM4TDS)
summary:
The treatment of cancer patients involves collecting and documenting a large amount of medical information, such as doctor’s notes, pathology findings, and radiology reports. At the University Hospital Dresden, medical documentation assistants (MDAs) enter this information manually into a structured system. However, with more and more patients and limited staff, the documentation process often remains incomplete. This can force doctors to search for missing information themselves, delaying treatment and creating extra work.

Researchers at the Else Kröner Fresenius Centre for Digital Health have developed a new software tool that uses artificial intelligence (AI) to improve this process. The tool, called LLM-AIx, can read free-text documents and suggest which information belongs in the structured system. Before the suggestions are saved, MDAs review and confirm them to ensure accuracy. The study follows a “human-in-the-loop” approach, meaning that all AI-generated outputs will be validated by trained medical documentation assistants before integration into the tumor documentation system.

The goal of this study is to evaluate how well the AI tool documents information compared to the current manual process. We will check the quality and completeness of the AI-suggested data to see if it meets the necessary standards. In addition, we will evaluate whether the tool helps MDAs in their daily work by saving time, reducing their workload and stress, and improving overall efficiency. By improving documentation quality and supporting MDAs, the AI tool may help doctors access information faster, leading to smoother and quicker patient care.

In addition to data quality and completeness, the study will also evaluate the user experience of medical documentation assistants (MDAs). This will be measured using the validated meCUE 2.0 questionnaire, Ecological Momentary Assessment (EMA), and physiological markers such as heart rate, heart rate variability, and electrodermal activity.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Patient data: Further processing of patients' medical documents required for tumour documentation for all patients being treated for tumours at the University Hospital/NCT Dresden. Consent in the form of the treatment contract and consent for recording in the tumour documentation system available. 
MDAs: Employment as MDA of the University Hospital Carl Gustav Carus Dresden and documentation using the tumour documentation system.
Exclusion criteria:
Patient data: Consent for recording in the tumour documentation system/treatment contract not available.
Exclusion criteria: Little knowledge of the German language.
